$$\forall C\in\mathbb{N},\ \varepsilon>0\ \exists K_4\ \forall n,k\in\mathbb{N}:\quad K_4<k,\ \ k^2\le C\cdot n\cdot\lfloor\log_2 k\rfloor,\ \ n<k^2 \implies \Bigl|\sum_{\substack{p \text{ prime}\\ k/2<p<11k/20}} \Bigl(\Bigl\{\frac{n}{p}\Bigr\}-\frac12\Bigr)\log p\Bigr| \le \varepsilon k$$

For every constant $C$ and every real $\varepsilon>0$ there is a threshold $K_4$ such that for all $k>K_4$ and all $n<k^2$ with $k^2\le C\,n\lfloor\log_2 k\rfloor$, the sum over primes $p$ with $k<2p$ and $20p<11k$ of $(\{n/p\}-\tfrac12)\log p$ has absolute value at most $\varepsilon k$. Here $\{n/p\}$ is `Int.fract` of the real quotient of the casts, $\log$ is `Real.log`, the sum runs over `Finset.range k` filtered by the three conditions, and the range hypotheses are in $\mathbb{N}$ where `Nat.log 2 k` is $\lfloor\log_2 k\rfloor$ (and $0$ for $k\le 1$), a natural number, so the right-hand side is a product of naturals.
label: Sander equidistribution: Σ({n/p} − 1/2) log p = o(k)
